Ensembles of models

Source: R/model-ensemble.R
ensemble.Rd

A mixture of the predictive distributions of several models: each draw of the ensemble is a draw of one component, chosen in proportion to the weights. Mixing draws (rather than averaging quantiles) keeps the paths coherent, so derived quantities such as life expectancy can be computed from the ensemble draws.

Usage

ensemble(..., weights = "equal", inner_origins = 3, inner_h = 5, top_k = NULL)

Arguments

...

Model specifications; names are used as labels.

weights

"equal", "crps", "stack" or a numeric vector.

inner_origins, inner_h

Inner backtest for weights = "crps" and weights = "stack", and for top_k.

top_k

Keep only the top_k components with the lowest CRPS in the inner backtest on the training years (the others get weight 0); NULL keeps all.

Value

A model specification.

Details

Weights:

  • "equal";

  • a numeric vector (normalised to sum to 1);

  • "crps": inverse mean CRPS of an inner rolling-origin backtest on the last inner_origins years of the training window, so the weights never use data after the forecast origin;

  • "stack": weights on the simplex that minimise the squared error of the weighted median forecasts (log scale) in the same inner backtest (the non-negative stacking, fitted on training data only).

Each draw of the ensemble comes from one component for all strata, so paths keep the dependence between strata and the coherence of reconciled components (reconciled()). A component that fails in a stratum is replaced there by the other components in proportion to their weights; this is recorded in the diagnostics. Any model specification can be a component, including joint models, Bayesian models, tuned, bootstrapped and reconciled models, and other ensembles.

A mixture is wider than its components when they disagree. In backtests on HMD data (England & Wales, France) and on the ONS deprivation data, Lee-Carter alone was too narrow (95% coverage 0.79 to 0.81), while an equal-weight mixture of lee_carter() and rwd() had 95% coverage of 0.92 to 0.98; its CRPS ranked second (France), third (England & Wales) and fifth of eight (ONS), close to the best model in each case (see the vignette "Comparison with demography, bamp and StMoMo"). In populations with few deaths per cell, use rwd(observation_noise = TRUE) as the random-walk component: the plain random walk accumulates the Poisson noise of observed rates and its long-horizon paths become implausible.

Examples

x <- mt_example(deaths = "single")
ens <- ensemble(lc = lee_carter(), rw = rwd())
fc <- mt_forecast(mt_fit(ens, x), h = 5, n_draws = 100, seed = 1)
